identity.name: ICRA Limited
identity.industry: Financial Services — Credit Rating Agency + BFSI Risk/Regulatory Analytics (RiskTech/RegTech) — NOT metadata

summary.oneLiner:
Strong headline growth (Q4 consolidated revenue +28.4% YoY, FY26 +20.4% YoY) is substantially Fintellix-driven
(R&A +56.8% YoY in Q4) rather than organic; the legacy high-margin KnowTech/Knowledge-Services book is
structurally moderating (automation + Moody's-parent in-sourcing + discontinued engagements), so the R&A
segment margin profile is shifting down as lower-margin, product-led BankTech/Fintellix/D2K businesses
(20-35% EBITDA range) become a bigger share of the mix. Management is opaque on Fintellix's standalone
economics and on M&A return discipline, drawing repeated analyst pushback.

one-line thesis: Strong headline growth (Q4 consolidated revenue +28.4% YoY, FY26 +20.4% YoY) is substantially Fintellix-driven
(R&A +56.8% YoY in Q4) rather than organic; the legacy high-margin KnowTech/Knowledge-Services book is
structurally moderating (automation + Moody's-parent in-sourcing + discontinued engagements), so the R&A
segment margin profile is shifting down as lower-margin, product-led BankTech/Fintellix/D2K businesses
(20-35% EBITDA range) become a bigger share of the mix. Management is opaque on Fintellix's standalone
economics and on M&A return discipline, drawing repeated analyst pushback.

> (2) Fintellix consolidated for only 6 months (Oct-2025 onward) in FY26 — FY27 will see a full first full-year
> consolidation, a mechanical growth tailwind independent of underlying Fintellix growth. (3) Dividend of
> INR 105/share includes a one-off INR 35/share special dividend for ICRA's 35th anniversary — not a run-rate payout.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue growth: No formal guidance given (repeatedly declined — "we don't give an outlook for revenue growth").
Directionally: Ratings to be driven by bank credit (bond-market activity expected subdued near-term on elevated
yields); no slowdown seen in Apr-May FY27 so far. R&A: Fintellix to "drive growth in the next 2-3 years" and
partly offset KnowTech moderation — magnitude explicitly not quantified.
Margin: No formal guidance ("we don't give a guidance on margin" — repeated for both Ratings and R&A/non-KS).
Directional color only: product-led BankTech-type businesses run 20-35% EBITDA (range driven by India vs.
developed-market revenue mix); Fintellix EBITDA ≈26% (disclosed in notes to accounts). Ratings segment expected
to keep expanding margin via operating leverage if double-digit revenue growth continues (employee cost growth
Order book / inflow target: n/a (no physical order book for this business).
Capex / commissioning dates: n/a — asset-light; no capex program disclosed. Investment focus is
product/tech platforms, AI tooling, and M&A integration (Fintellix, D2K).
Macro house-view (relevant to Ratings pipeline): ICRA's own FY27 GDP growth call = 6.2% real terms
(assumes ~$95/bbl average crude), citing West Asia conflict energy-price shock (bigger FY27 impact expected
vs. FY26) and El Nino/weak-monsoon risk to rural demand in H2.
Regulatory trigger to watch: banks' transition to Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework effective 1-Apr-2027
— explicitly flagged as a structural demand driver for risk-modeling/compliance solutions (BankTech/Fintellix).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable — ratings/analytics business model, no backlog metric disclosed. Qualitative pipeline color:
management believes the BankTech/CapTech product portfolio is "pretty much complete" with a "few gaps" being
built internally; will pursue adjacencies beyond the existing credit-value-stream/data-value-stream focus via
internal investment rather than acquisitions going forward (per Shailendra M., in response to Gokul Maheshwari).
segment / subsidiary detail: Ratings (standalone-led): steady double-digit trajectory (Q4 +10.6%, FY26 +14.2% YoY), broadly in line with
peers per management ("similar band as several of our peers... different base to contend with"); strategy =
focus on growth segments within bank credit vs. bonds, playing interest-rate/yield cycles.
Research & Analytics (R&A) — restructured this year into 3 sub-verticals under a unified IT/product
engineering organization:
KnowTech (formerly "Knowledge Services" — Moody's-parent outsourcing): muted/moderating growth — driven
by discontinued engagements, increasing automation, and periodic Moody's in-sourcing of processes; "we don't
expect higher double-digit growth there" going forward.
BankTech: erstwhile RMS (Risk Management Solutions) + Fintellix + D2K combined into one integrated
division; product-led, 20-35% EBITDA range; cross-sell/synergy realization from D2K + Fintellix expected to
"play out over the next 2 years."
CapTech: capital-markets analytics — asset managers + newer capital-market segments; driven by both
regulatory tightening and "greenfield" opportunities.
Ex-Fintellix, FY26 R&A growth was muted at the KnowTech level but the smaller RMS/Market-data businesses
"grew... and turned profitable" even on a small base (Shailendra M.).
Fintellix (acquired, consolidated from Oct-2025 = H2FY26 only): a RiskTech/RegTech platform — two solution
families: (1) regulatory data-repository/reporting (structuring bank transaction/analytical data into
regulator-mandated formats/APIs), and (2) credit-analytics (early-warning signals, NPA monitoring/classification,
incurred-loss and ECL-method credit-loss accounting). Does not compete with core-banking vendors
(Finacle/Oracle FSS/Intellect) — sits on top of/consumes data from them. Global competitors: Regnology and
Nasdaq Technologies (both PE/public-backed roll-ups, not India-listed). ~26% EBITDA margin (per notes to
accounts). Preferred commercial model is annuity/subscription; market still transitioning from upfront-license.
Leadership change: Shailendra Mruthyunjayappa became CEO of ICRA Analytics and head of the entire R&A
vertical (KnowTech + BankTech + CapTech), succeeding Jayanta Chatterjee, who retired Jan-2026.
D2K Technologies: acquired ~2 years ago; deeper integration into the combined BankTech product suite only
happening now, in tandem with Fintellix onboarding; management declined to give D2K-specific margin color.
growth verticals / optionality: Geographic mix shift (India → developed markets) within product businesses is a margin lever — 20-35% EBITDA
range is driven largely by geography mix.
Cross-sell across the combined BankTech suite (RMS + Fintellix + D2K) into overlapping large-bank customers —
multi-product penetration expected to build over the next 2 years.
AI: deploying AI-powered agents in internal processes and embedding an AI layer into subsidiary analytical
tools; management view is AI augments rather than disrupts this business given regulatory-interpretation
complexity (see §6a).
ECL-framework transition (1-Apr-2027) and ongoing capital-market regulatory evolution are structural, dated
demand drivers for BankTech/Fintellix.
M&A: management explicitly evaluates further capital-allocation options / acquisitions using an internal
IRR/payback framework (not disclosed publicly) — cash pile (>INR 700 cr) gives optionality.
6a. moat & competitive position: Regulatory/domain-expertise moat for the RiskTech/RegTech (Fintellix) line: management explicitly argues
this space is comparatively insulated from AI disruption because "the level of accuracy required, the level of
SME expertise... to interpret the regulations and construct those regulatory submissions... is quite high" —
an external-provider expertise advantage over in-house/generic-AI builds.
35-year rating franchise / credibility: FY26 marked ICRA's 35th year of operations, cited as underpinning
"analytical rigor and market relevance" — standard ratings-agency reputational moat, not new evidence but
reaffirmed this call (also drove the special dividend).
Non-compete positioning vs. core-banking vendors (Finacle/Oracle FSS/Intellect Design) — Fintellix sits as an
analytics layer on top of/complementary to those systems rather than competing head-on, reducing direct
competitive intensity from that adjacent software category.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 consolidated PBT growth (+10%, ex-Labor-Code exceptional) lagged revenue growth (+20.4%) — clear evidence
of margin dilution from business mix shift (higher share of lower-margin non-KnowTech/product revenue).
Ratings segment: margin expansion via operating leverage — management's rule of thumb is that double-digit
ratings revenue growth typically outpaces employee-cost growth (sub-10%), generating margin "pass-through."
R&A segment: KnowTech (higher-margin, outsourcing-style) shrinking as a share of mix; BankTech/Fintellix
(20-35% EBITDA, product-led but different, more variable margin profile by geography) growing share — net
effect is segment-level margin moderation, management declines to size it or give a stabilization timeline.
Vs. domestic ratings peers ("the other 2 CRAs"), management acknowledges "there is a margin difference" and
intends to close it via sales scale-up, but gives no quantification or date.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No physical capex program — business is asset-light. Investment is in technology/product platforms
(AI tooling, compliance capability, delivery frameworks) and in integrating acquired businesses (Fintellix, D2K).
No slippage risk of the traditional capex/commissioning kind to track.
capital allocation: Dividend raised: normal dividend increased from INR 60/share (historical run-rate) to INR 70/share, plus a
one-off INR 35/share special dividend marking 35 years of operations → INR 105/share total this year
(subject to shareholder approval). Management has "consistently increased dividend payout" over the last
3 years.
Net cash >INR 700 cr on balance sheet; guided FCF generation of INR 180-200 cr/year — cash pile will keep
growing absent redeployment.
No buyback announced. Management response to a direct buyback question was non-committal: "we keep on
continuing to look at those options especially considering... changes to taxation rules... as and when the
Board approves, we will relook at capital allocation further." A shareholder (Gokul Maheshwari) explicitly
urged the company to "rethink ways to actually give money back to shareholders" given the non-capital-intensive
model — met only with "Point noted."
M&A discipline not disclosed publicly: management confirmed an internal IRR/payback framework exists and is
Board-reviewed periodically, but repeatedly declined (under sustained analyst pressure from Ravi Purohit) to
share benchmarks or post-acquisition scorecards publicly, unlike global peers (Moody's/S&P), citing internal
Board governance as sufficient. This was flagged by the analyst as a shareholder-disclosure gap.
Fintellix acquisition size referenced by an analyst as ~$25mn (not confirmed/denied by management on the call).
risks & watch-items: Macro: West Asia conflict → elevated global energy/commodity prices, expected to weigh more heavily on
India GDP in early FY27 than it did in Q4FY26; ICRA's own house view is FY27 real GDP growth moderating to
6.2% (crude ~$95/bbl assumption) — a downside risk if the conflict/oil-price shock persists longer than assumed.
El Nino / weak monsoon forecast — dulls agri/rural outlook for H2FY27, a read-through to bank credit demand
in rural-linked segments.
Bond-market activity likely to stay subdued near-term on elevated yields — a headwind to the Ratings segment
(bank credit is expected to offset, per management, but this is a relative-mix bet, not a guarantee).
KnowTech/Knowledge-Services structural decline: automation + discontinued engagements + periodic Moody's
parent in-sourcing → "we don't expect higher double-digit growth"; this is ICRA's traditionally highest-margin
R&A business, so continued erosion here compounds the margin mix-shift risk.
Margin-mix dilution in R&A not quantified or timelined by management — a genuine unknown for modeling
purposes going into FY27.
Disclosure opacity / governance flag: management declined, across multiple analyst attempts in this call,
to disclose (a) Fintellix's standalone profit contribution beyond the ~26% EBITDA note, (b) acquisition-level
IRR/payback outcomes for D2K/Fintellix, citing shareholder-parity concerns — an explicit and repeated point of
friction with the buy-side on this call, worth monitoring for future disclosure improvement or persistence.
management quality / tone: Confident and steady-state in tone, but consistently declines to give forward guidance on revenue or margins for
either segment — a deliberate, repeated stance ("we don't give... guidance") rather than an evasive one-off.
Became visibly guarded under sustained, specific analyst pressure (Ravi Purohit) on acquisition-return disclosure
and Fintellix segment economics, ultimately just reiterating that Board-level oversight exists without committing
to any public disclosure upgrade. Capital-allocation feedback (buyback ask) was acknowledged but not committed to.
Reasonably transparent, by contrast, about the structural R&A margin mix-shift and KnowTech moderation — did not
oversell Fintellix's near-term contribution and was explicit that ex-Fintellix R&A growth was muted.
non-obvious takeaways: FY26's headline growth is substantially an inorganic/base effect: Fintellix was consolidated for only H2FY26
(Oct-2025 onward), so FY27 will see a full first full year of Fintellix consolidation — a mechanical
growth tailwind into FY27 numbers independent of any underlying improvement in Fintellix's own growth rate.
Watch for this base effect when assessing FY27 R&A growth headlines.
~USD 18mn (≈"a shade below one-third") of FY26 revenue is USD-denominated with predominantly rupee-denominated
costs — a natural currency tailwind/margin lever from INR depreciation with limited offsetting USD cost drag.
The R&A reorganization into KnowTech/BankTech/CapTech under one unified IT/product-engineering org signals a
structural pivot from a legacy outsourcing/Knowledge-Services model toward a product-led, annuity/subscription
RiskTech-RegTech model — a multi-year business-model transition, not just a cosmetic segment relabeling.
The ECL framework transition for Indian banks (effective 1-Apr-2027) is a clean, dated regulatory catalyst
explicitly named by management as a demand driver — a concrete date to track for BankTech/Fintellix inflection.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis: No company-specific supply-chain/procurement challenges were discussed on this call (services/analytics business,
not a physical value chain). The macro headwinds raised (West Asia conflict/oil-price shock, El Nino/weak
monsoon, elevated bond yields) are broad-market risks, not challenges specific to named listed counterparties.
Fintellix's named competitors (Regnology, Nasdaq Technologies) are foreign/unlisted-in-India; domestic ratings
peers were referenced only generically ("the other 2 CRAs," "other CRAs") without naming CRISIL/CARE/India
Ratings on the call, so per the no-inference rule this is left unresolved rather than guessed.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4FY26 (this): Reported Q4 consol. revenue +28.4% YoY / FY26 +20.4% YoY, R&A growth substantially
Fintellix-driven (H2-only consolidation); FY26 PBT +10% YoY (ex-Labor-Code exceptional) — margin dilution vs.
revenue growth; special 35th-anniversary dividend of INR 105/share total; no buyback despite >INR 700 cr net
cash; management declined to disclose Fintellix segment economics or M&A return metrics publicly.
Q1FY27 → check: Does Fintellix's first full-quarter-of-full-year-run-rate show the expected
growth contribution (watch for FY27 base-effect commentary)? Any slippage in KnowTech decline vs. "moderation"
framing? Did GDP-linked bond-market softness materialize into slower Ratings growth (watch Apr-May trend
commentary vs. actuals)? Any move on buyback/capital-return given continued cash build? Any incremental
disclosure on Fintellix profitability given repeated analyst pressure this quarter?
